Data

ACS-5
```{r}
years <- c(2019, 2020, 2021, 2023, 2024)

my_vars <- c(
  # Population & demographics
  tot_pop       = "B01003_001",
  median_age    = "B01002_001",
  white         = "C02003_003",
  black         = "C02003_004",
  asian         = "C02003_006",
  hispanic      = "B03001_003",

  # Economic wellbeing
  medhhinc      = "B25119_001",
  pop_poverty   = "B17001_002",
  pop_poverty_universe = "B17001_001",
  labor_force   = "B23025_003",
  unemployed    = "B23025_005",

  # Housing
  hu_ownocc     = "B25003_002",
  tot_hu        = "B25001_001",
  rent_burden_30_35   = "B25070_007",  # 30.0-34.9%
  rent_burden_35_40   = "B25070_008",  # 35.0-39.9%
  rent_burden_40_50   = "B25070_009",  # 40.0-49.9%
  rent_burden_50plus  = "B25070_010",  # 50.0%+
  rent_total          = "B25070_001",

  # Education
  edu_hs_or_less     = "B15003_017",
  edu_bachelors_plus = "B15003_022",
  edu_total          = "B15003_001",

  # Family structure
  divorced_m    = "B12001_010",
  divorced_f    = "B12001_019",
  single_dad_children = "B11003_010",   # male householder, no wife, with own children <18
  single_mom_children = "B11003_016"   # female householder, no husband, with own children <18

)

# Pulling the Census variables for New York State, at the county level
census_data_nys <- map_dfr(
  years,
  ~ get_acs(
      geography = "county",
      variables = my_vars,
      state = "NY",
      year = .x,
      survey = "acs5",
      geometry = FALSE,
      cache_table = TRUE
    ) %>%
    mutate(year = .x)
  ) %>%
  select(GEOID, NAME, variable, estimate, year) %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = variable, values_from = estimate) %>%
  arrange(NAME, year)

census_data_nys <- census_data_nys %>%
  mutate(divorced = divorced_m + divorced_f)
```

Prisons (ICPSR)
```{r}
#US Prisons (from ICPSR)
#The raw dataset contains 6,468 prison facilities with geographic boundaries.
#Three filters are applied: (1) only facilities with STATUS "OPEN" or "CLOSED" are
#retained, dropping ambiguous or unknown statuses; (2) TYPE "COUNTY" is excluded,
#removing local jails which were not sited as economic development tools and do not
#fit the theoretical framework of the study; (3) restricted to New York State.
#The cleaned dataset is then collapsed to the county level using COUNTYFIPS,
#producing counts and capacity/population totals broken out by status (open, closed, and combined).
prisons_icpsr <- st_read("data/prison-boundaries-1-geojson.geojson")
#names(prisons_icpsr)

prisons_clean_nys <- prisons_icpsr %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  filter(
    STATUS %in% c("OPEN", "CLOSED"),
    TYPE != "COUNTY",
    STATE == "NY"
  )

prisons_by_county_nys <- prisons_clean_nys %>%
  group_by(COUNTYFIPS) %>%
  summarise(
    num_prisons        = n(),
    num_open           = sum(STATUS == "OPEN"),
    num_closed         = sum(STATUS == "CLOSED"),
    capacity_total     = sum(CAPACITY, na.rm = TRUE),
    capacity_open      = sum(CAPACITY[STATUS == "OPEN"],   na.rm = TRUE),
    capacity_closed    = sum(CAPACITY[STATUS == "CLOSED"], na.rm = TRUE),
    pop_total          = sum(POPULATION, na.rm = TRUE),
    pop_open           = sum(POPULATION[STATUS == "OPEN"],   na.rm = TRUE),
    pop_closed         = sum(POPULATION[STATUS == "CLOSED"], na.rm = TRUE)
  )

```

Death counts
```{r}
#death counts and death rates for drug overdose, suicide, homicide and firearm injuries by county of residence

#The raw dataset contains county-level death counts and rates for drug overdose,
#firearm injuries, homicide, and suicide across multiple years. The data is filtered
#to 2019 and restricted to three Intent categories relevant to the distress index:
#Drug_OD, All_Suicide, and All_Homicide. Firearm-specific subcategories (FA_Suicide,
#FA_Homicide, FA_Deaths) are dropped to avoid double-counting, as they are subsets
#of the all-cause homicide and suicide totals. Rate is coerced to numeric, and the
#dataset is pivoted to wide format so each county appears as a single row with
#separate rate columns for each outcome. Small cell counts (1-9 deaths) reported
#as ranges by the CDC are handled by using the pre-computed Rate column directly,
#bypassing the suppression issue in the Count column entirely.


injury_overdose_violence <- read_csv("data/injury_overdose_violence.csv")


#2019-2024
injury_overdose_violence_nys <- injury_overdose_violence %>%
  filter(ST_NAME == "New York") %>%
  filter(Period %in% c("2019", "2020", "2021", "2023", "2024")) %>%   
  filter(Intent %in% c("Drug_OD", "All_Suicide", "All_Homicide")) %>%
  mutate(Rate = as.numeric(Rate)) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols    = c(GEOID, NAME, ST_GEOID, ST_NAME, Period),   
    names_from = Intent,
    values_from = Rate,
    names_glue = "{Intent}_rate"
  ) %>%
  rename(
    overdose_rate = Drug_OD_rate,
    suicide_rate  = All_Suicide_rate,
    homicide_rate = All_Homicide_rate,
    year = Period
  )


```

Unemployment (BLS)
```{r}
#BLS (unemployment rate)

# The raw BLS county unemployment file for 2019 is structured with the title row
# as the first row and the actual column headers as the second row, a common BLS
# formatting issue. The column names are manually assigned via set_names(), and the
# spurious header row is dropped with slice(-1). Trailing footnote rows are removed
# by filtering out blank state FIPS values. State and county FIPS codes, stored in
# separate columns in the raw file, are padded to 2 and 3 digits respectively and
# concatenated into a single 5-digit GEOID to match the join key used across all
# other datasets. All numeric columns are coerced from character, and the dataset
# is reduced to the GEOID, county name, and core labor force variables.

unemployment_2019 <- read_excel("data/unemployment19.xlsx")

unemployment_2019_clean <- unemployment_2019 %>%
  set_names(c("laus_code", "state_fips", "county_fips", 
              "county_name", "year", "labor_force", 
              "employed", "unemployed", "unemp_rate")) %>%
  slice(-1) %>%                                        
  filter(!is.na(state_fips), state_fips != "") %>%     
  mutate(
    GEOID     = paste0(
                  str_pad(state_fips,  2, pad = "0"),
                  str_pad(county_fips, 3, pad = "0")
                ),
    unemp_rate = as.numeric(unemp_rate),
    labor_force = as.numeric(labor_force),
    employed    = as.numeric(employed),
    unemployed  = as.numeric(unemployed)
  ) %>%
  select(GEOID, county_name, labor_force, employed, unemployed, unemp_rate)
```

Life Expectancy (from CDC, 2010-2015)

```{r}
# Life expectancy data comes from the USALEEP project (2010-2015), the most
# comprehensive source of county-level life expectancy available for the contiguous
# US. The raw file is at the census tract level, so it must be aggregated to the
# county level. Rather than a simple mean, a population-weighted mean is computed
# so that more populous tracts contribute proportionally more to the county estimate.
# Tract-level population denominators are pulled from the 2011-2015 ACS 5-year
# estimates (variable B01003_001) via tidycensus, restricted to New York State only.
# A county FIPS crosswalk is constructed from the built-in fips_codes dataframe in
# tidycensus and joined to the life expectancy file on county name. Tract numbers
# in the USALEEP file (e.g. "0201.00") are reformatted into standard 11-digit Census
# GEOIDs by removing the decimal point, padding to 6 digits, and prepending the
# 5-digit county FIPS code. The 2010-2015 vintage is used as it is the only
# nationally comprehensive county-level life expectancy dataset available; this
# measurement lag relative to the outcome year(s) is acknowledged as a limitation.

life_expectancy <- read_csv("data/life_expectancy_2010-2015.csv")

# Pull tract-level population for New York only (state FIPS "36"), no loop needed
tract_pop <- get_acs(
  geography = "tract",
  variables = c(tract_pop = "B01003_001"),
  state     = "NY",
  year      = 2015,
  survey    = "acs5",
  geometry  = FALSE
) %>%
  select(GEOID, tract_pop = estimate)

fips_xwalk <- fips_codes %>%
  filter(state == "NY") %>%
  mutate(
    county_full = paste0(county, ", ", state),
    county_fips = paste0(state_code, county_code)
  ) %>%
  select(county_full, county_fips)

life_expectancy_clean <- life_expectancy %>%
  janitor::clean_names() %>%
  filter(county != "(blank)", !is.na(census_tract_number)) %>%
  left_join(fips_xwalk, by = c("county" = "county_full")) %>%
  filter(!is.na(county_fips)) %>%     # drops all non-NY counties, since they won't match the NY-only crosswalk
  mutate(
    tract_clean = str_remove(census_tract_number, "\\.") %>%
                  str_pad(6, pad = "0"),
    GEOID = paste0(county_fips, tract_clean)
  )

life_expectancy_county_nys <- life_expectancy_clean %>%
  left_join(tract_pop, by = "GEOID") %>%
  group_by(county_fips, state, county) %>%
  summarise(
    life_exp_weighted = weighted.mean(life_expectancy,
                                      w     = tract_pop,
                                      na.rm = TRUE),
    n_tracts = n()
  ) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  rename(GEOID = county_fips)
```


Occupation - Correctional Institution
```{r}
correctional_employment_2019 <- read_csv("data/correctional_employment_2019.csv")
correctional_employment_2020 <- read_csv("data/correctional_employment_2020.csv")
correctional_employment_2021 <- read_csv("data/correctional_employment_2021.csv")
correctional_employment_2022 <- read_csv("data/correctional_employment_2022.csv")
correctional_employment_2023 <- read_csv("data/correctional_employment_2023.csv")
correctional_employment_2024 <- read_csv("data/correctional_employment_2024.csv")


# QCEW correctional employment (NAICS 92214), 2019
# Due to disclosure suppression affecting 88% of county-level records,
# employment is coded as a three-category variable rather than a continuous measure.

library(dplyr)
library(purrr)
library(tidyr)

years_needed <- c(2019, 2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024)

# Map each year to its correct county-level agglvl_code
# (77 for years where QCEW used the older scheme, 78 for 2024's new scheme)
agglvl_lookup <- c(
  "2019" = 77,
  "2020" = 77,
  "2021" = 77,
  "2022" = 77,
  "2023" = 77,
  "2024" = 78
)

occupation_nys_19_24 <- map_dfr(years_needed, function(yr) {
  file_path <- paste0("data/correctional_employment_", yr, ".csv")
  occ_raw <- read_csv(file_path, show_col_types = FALSE)
  
  target_code <- agglvl_lookup[[as.character(yr)]]

  occ_raw %>%
    filter(
      agglvl_code == target_code,
      substr(area_fips, 1, 2) == "36"
    ) %>%
    group_by(area_fips) %>%
    summarise(
      correctional_emplvl = sum(annual_avg_emplvl, na.rm = TRUE),
      any_suppressed      = any(disclosure_code == "N"),
      any_reported        = any(is.na(disclosure_code) & annual_avg_emplvl > 0),
      .groups = "drop"
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      corr_employ_cat = case_when(
        any_reported   ~ "reported",
        any_suppressed ~ "suppressed",
        TRUE           ~ "none"
      ),
      year = yr
    ) %>%
    rename(GEOID = area_fips)
})

nrow(occupation_nys_19_24)
table(occupation_nys_19_24$year)
```


##Domestic Violence
```{r}
#2019-2024
nys_violence_2019_raw <- read_excel("data/nys_violence_2019.xls")
nys_violence_2020_raw <- read_excel("data/nys_violence_2020.xls")
nys_violence_2021_raw <- read_excel("data/nys_violence_2021.xls")
nys_violence_2022_raw <- read_excel("data/nys_violence_2022.xls")
nys_violence_2023_raw <- read_excel("data/nys_violence_2023.xls")
nys_violence_2024_raw <- read_excel("data/nys_violence_2024.xlsx")

nys_violence_2019 <- nys_violence_2019_raw %>%
  rename(
    county = 1,
    offense_type = 2,
    female_intimate_partner = 3,
    male_intimate_partner = 4,
    total_intimate_partner = 5,
    other_family_victim = 6,
    total_all_victims = 7
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(c(female_intimate_partner:total_all_victims), as.numeric))

nys_violence_2019 <- nys_violence_2019 %>%
  fill(county)  

nys_violence_2019 <- nys_violence_2019 %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(female_intimate_partner, male_intimate_partner, other_family_victim),
    names_to = "victim_type",
    values_to = "count"
  )

nys_violence_2019 <- nys_violence_2019 %>%
  filter(!is.na(county), !county %in% c("DOMESTIC VIOLENCE VICTIMS REPORTED IN 2019", "NON-NEW YORK CITY COUNTIES"))

nys_violence_2019 <- nys_violence_2019 %>%
  mutate(year = 2019)

nys_violence_2019 <- nys_violence_2019 %>%
  slice(1:(n() - 21))
```

```{r}
nys_violence_all <- map_dfr(years_needed, function(yr) {
  ext <- if (yr == 2024) "xlsx" else "xls"
  file_path <- paste0("data/nys_violence_", yr, ".", ext)
  raw <- read_excel(file_path)
  
  raw %>%
    rename(
      county = 1,
      offense_type = 2,
      female_intimate_partner = 3,
      male_intimate_partner = 4,
      total_intimate_partner = 5,
      other_family_victim = 6,
      total_all_victims = 7
    ) %>%
    mutate(across(c(female_intimate_partner:total_all_victims), as.numeric)) %>%
    fill(county) %>%
    pivot_longer(
      cols = c(female_intimate_partner, male_intimate_partner, other_family_victim),
      names_to = "victim_type",
      values_to = "count"
    ) %>%
    filter(
      !is.na(county),
      !grepl("DOMESTIC VIOLENCE VICTIMS REPORTED IN", county),
      county != "NON-NEW YORK CITY COUNTIES"
    ) %>%
    mutate(year = yr)
})

nys_violence_wide <- nys_violence_all %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(county, year),
    names_from = c(offense_type, victim_type),
    values_from = count,
    names_glue = "{offense_type}_{victim_type}"
  )
```

##Staffing levels and suicides
```{r}
library(readr)
library(dplyr)
library(lubridate)

staffing_levels_nys <- read_csv("data/staffing_levels_nys.csv")
suicides_nys <- read_csv("data/suicides_nys.csv")

# --- SUICIDES ---
suicides_matched <- suicides_nys %>%
  mutate(facility_name_clean = trimws(toupper(FACILITY_NAME))) %>%
  mutate(matched_name = facility_crosswalk[facility_name_clean]) %>%
  left_join(ny_facility_lookup_full, by = c("matched_name" = "name_clean")) %>%
  filter(SUICIDE_YEAR >= 2019, SUICIDE_YEAR <= 2024)

sum(is.na(suicides_matched$COUNTYFIPS))   # check match rate

suicides_by_county_year <- suicides_matched %>%
  group_by(COUNTYFIPS, COUNTY, SUICIDE_YEAR) %>%
  summarise(n_suicides = n(), .groups = "drop") %>%
  rename(GEOID = COUNTYFIPS, county_name = COUNTY, year = SUICIDE_YEAR)

# --- STAFFING ---
staffing_matched <- staffing_levels_nys %>%
  mutate(
    facility_name_clean = trimws(toupper(FACILITY_NAME)),
    report_year = year(ymd(REPORT_DATE))
  ) %>%
  mutate(matched_name = facility_crosswalk[facility_name_clean]) %>%
  left_join(ny_facility_lookup_full, by = c("matched_name" = "name_clean")) %>%
  filter(report_year >= 2019, report_year <= 2024, STAFFING_CATEGORY == "TOTAL")

sum(is.na(staffing_matched$COUNTYFIPS))

staffing_by_county_year <- staffing_matched %>%
  group_by(COUNTYFIPS, COUNTY, report_year) %>%
  summarise(
    budgeted_fill = sum(BUDGETED_FILL_LEVEL, na.rm = TRUE),
    actual_fill   = sum(ACTUAL_FILL_LEVEL, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  rename(GEOID = COUNTYFIPS, county_name = COUNTY, year = report_year)
```

##Final Dataset
```{r}
library(dplyr)

# Rename each static file's GEOID-equivalent column to GEOID for consistency
prisons_static <- prisons_by_county_nys %>% rename(GEOID = COUNTYFIPS)
rural_static <- rural_2023_nys %>% rename(GEOID = FIPS)   # adjust if the actual column name differs
life_exp_static <- life_expectancy_county_nys              # already has GEOID

# Build the master year x county panel starting from ACS, since it's your most complete file
master_nys <- census_data_nys %>%
  left_join(injury_overdose_violence_nys %>% mutate(year = as.numeric(year)), by = c("GEOID", "year")) %>%
  left_join(occupation_nys_19_24, by = c("GEOID", "year")) %>%
  left_join(deaths_by_county_year, by = c("GEOID", "year")) %>%
  left_join(suicides_by_county_year, by = c("GEOID", "year")) %>%
  left_join(staffing_by_county_year, by = c("GEOID", "year")) %>%
  left_join(prisons_static, by = "GEOID") %>%
  left_join(rural_static, by = "GEOID") %>%
  left_join(life_exp_static, by = "GEOID")
```

```{r}
    pct_hispanic = hispanic / tot_pop
  ) %>%
  # other proportions

    pct_poverty     = pop_povstat / tot_pop,
    homeown_rate    = hu_ownocc   / tot_hu,
    divorce_rate    = divorced    / tot_pop
  ) %>%
  # population density would need area — do you have that?

    log_pop      = log(tot_pop),
    log_medhhinc = log(medhhinc)
  )
```

```{r}
    suicides_in_custody_rate = n_suicides / tot_pop * 100000,

    # Domestic violence, per 100k population
    dv_total_rate = (Total_female_intimate_partner + Total_male_intimate_partner + Total_other_family_victim) / tot_pop * 100000,
    dv_agg_assault_rate = (`Agg Assault_female_intimate_partner` + `Agg Assault_male_intimate_partner` + `Agg Assault_other_family_victim`) / tot_pop * 100000,
    dv_sex_offense_rate = (`Sex Offense_female_intimate_partner` + `Sex Offense_male_intimate_partner` + `Sex Offense_other_family_victim`) / tot_pop * 100000,

    # Correctional employment, per 100k population (only meaningful where reported, not suppressed)
    correctional_emplvl_rate = correctional_emplvl / tot_pop * 100000,

    # Prison staffing gap, as % understaffed relative to budget
    staffing_gap_pct = (budgeted_fill - actual_fill) / budgeted_fill,

    # Economic/demographic percentages
    poverty_rate     = pop_poverty / pop_poverty_universe,
    unemp_rate        = unemployed / labor_force,
    pct_white         = white / tot_pop,
    pct_black         = black / tot_pop,
    pct_asian         = asian / tot_pop,
    pct_hispanic      = hispanic / tot_pop,
    homeown_rate      = hu_ownocc / tot_hu,
    pct_bachelors_plus = edu_bachelors_plus / edu_total,
    pct_hs_or_less     = edu_hs_or_less / edu_total,
    divorce_rate       = divorced / tot_pop,
    rent_burdened_30plus_rate = (rent_burden_30_35 + rent_burden_35_40 + rent_burden_40_50 + rent_burden_50plus) / rent_total,
    single_parent_rate = (single_dad_children + single_mom_children) / tot_hu   # or divide by tot_pop, depending on definition you want

  )
```

```{r}
library(gt)
packageVersion("gt")

vars_to_test <- c(
  dv_total_rate = "DV Rate (Total)",
  dv_female_rate = "DV Rate (Female victims)",
  dv_male_rate = "DV Rate (Male victims)",
  dv_agg_assault_rate = "DV Rate (Agg. Assault)",
  dv_sex_offense_rate = "DV Rate (Sex Offense)",
  suicide_rate = "Suicide Rate (community)",
  overdose_rate = "Overdose Rate",
  homicide_rate = "Homicide Rate",
  life_exp_weighted = "Life Expectancy",
  divorce_rate = "Divorce Rate",
  medhhinc = "Median HH Income",
  poverty_rate = "Poverty Rate",
  unemp_rate = "Unemployment Rate",
  homeown_rate = "Homeownership Rate",
  pct_bachelors_plus = "% Bachelor's+",
  single_parent_rate = "Single-Parent Rate"
)

results <- lapply(names(vars_to_test), function(v) {
  d <- master_nys %>% filter(!is.na(.data[[v]]), !is.na(prison_present))
  t_result <- t.test(d[[v]] ~ d$prison_present)
  
  tibble(
    variable = vars_to_test[[v]],
    mean_no_prison = t_result$estimate[1],
    mean_prison = t_result$estimate[2],
    difference = t_result$estimate[2] - t_result$estimate[1],
    p_value = t_result$p.value
  )
}) %>% bind_rows()

results %>%
  gt() %>%
  cols_label(
    variable = "Variable",
    mean_no_prison = "No Prison",
    mean_prison = "Prison Present",
    difference = "Difference",
    p_value = "p-value"
  ) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = c(mean_no_prison, mean_prison, difference), decimals = 3) %>%
  fmt_number(columns = p_value, decimals = 4) %>%
  tab_header(
    title = "NY County Outcomes by Prison Presence",
    subtitle = "Two-sample t-tests, county-year observations, 2019-2024"
  ) %>%
  tab_style(
    style = cell_fill(color = "#fff3cd"),
    locations = cells_body(rows = p_value < 0.05)
  ) %>%
  tab_footnote(
    footnote = "County-year panel; standard errors do not account for repeated observations per county over time.",
    locations = cells_column_labels(columns = p_value)
  )
```

```{r}
  slice(1:(n() - 21))
```

```{r}
#2020
nys_violence_2020_raw <- read_excel("data/nys_violence_2020.xls")

nys_violence_2020 <- nys_violence_2020_raw %>%
  rename(
    county = 1,
    offense_type = 2,
    female_intimate_partner = 3,
    male_intimate_partner = 4,
    total_intimate_partner = 5,
    other_family_victim = 6,
    total_all_victims = 7
  ) %>%
  mutate(across(c(female_intimate_partner:total_all_victims), as.numeric))

nys_violence_2020 <- nys_violence_2020 %>%
  fill(county)  

nys_violence_2020 <- nys_violence_2020 %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(female_intimate_partner, male_intimate_partner, other_family_victim),
    names_to = "victim_type",
    values_to = "count"
  )

nys_violence_2020 <- nys_violence_2020 %>%
  filter(!is.na(county), !county %in% c("DOMESTIC VIOLENCE VICTIMS REPORTED IN 2020", "NON-NEW YORK CITY COUNTIES"))

nys_violence_2020 <- nys_violence_2020 %>%
  mutate(year = 2020)

nys_violence_2020 <- nys_violence_2020 %>%
  slice(1:(n() - 21))
```
